newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise after U.S. jobs report.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise after U.S. jobs report.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late morning Friday, boosted by a U.S. jobless report seen to reduce the chances of a hike in U.S. interest rates in July.
"The market is very strong," said a trader at a local bank, adding that activity was busy.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 3/8 at 94 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.15 at 123.90.

Although traders agreed the U.S. jobless report gave mixed signals, with the unemployment rate falling to its lowest level in 23 years while jobs growth slowed, on balance players viewed the report as reducing the likelihood of a U.S. rate hike.
"There was a double message in the report but apparently it makes it less likely of a rate hike" in July, said another trader.
